title: Clean Code Exercises
description: Practise the ideas from this Clean Code course. Each answer has an explanation to help you learn.

exercises.question: Which name explains the value better?
exercises.explanation: Code is read many times. A clear name explains the purpose of a value without making the reader solve a puzzle. The result is 4. The name tells us what is being counted.

exercises.question: Which function name is clearer?
exercises.explanation: Function names should explain what the action does. A reader should not need to inspect every line to understand a call. The result is 7. The function name says it adds prices.

exercises.question: What is this function's job?
exercises.explanation: A small function with one clear job is easier to test and reuse. Separate a calculation from drawing a page. The result is 5. This function calculates a total and does not change the page.

exercises.question: What does MAX_BOOKS explain?
exercises.explanation: A named constant explains why a special value appears. It also gives the rule one clear place to change. The result is true. The name explains why 3 is used in the rule.

exercises.question: Which case returns early?
exercises.explanation: A guard clause handles a special case early. It can reduce deep nesting and make the main path easier to follow. The result is Hello!. The empty-name case ends before the normal greeting.

exercises.question: Why share this function?
exercises.explanation: When the same rule appears in several places, changes can be missed. Put a shared rule in one clear function. The output is false true. Both checks use the same passing rule.

exercises.question: What should a useful comment explain?
options: Only repeat the next word of code
exercises.explanation: A useful comment explains why a choice was made. The code should already explain ordinary steps through names. The result is 0. The comment explains why a starting value is present.

exercises.question: Which message helps a caller fix the input?
options: Age must be a whole number of zero or more
exercises.explanation: An error should say what input was wrong or what action failed. It should not expose private details. The result is 10. Invalid ages would get a message that explains the rule.

exercises.question: What must be true to join?
exercises.explanation: A condition is easier to read when it states one clear question. Name a complicated condition if its purpose is not obvious. The result is false because both conditions must be true.

exercises.question: Why make a copy before sort?
exercises.explanation: A function that returns a new value can be easier to reason about than one that changes its input. Make changes clear in the function name or contract. The original stays 3,1,2; the copy becomes 1,2,3.

exercises.question: What should refactoring preserve?
exercises.explanation: Refactoring improves the code structure while keeping the same intended behaviour. Tests help check that the behaviour stayed the same. The result is true for this input. More useful cases would strengthen the check.

exercises.question: What is the stated purpose of trimTitle?
exercises.explanation: A focused review checks whether a change solves its stated problem and keeps the code readable. Small changes are easier to inspect. The check passes. The change has one purpose: removing spaces at the ends.
